line: Jung on earth: as fourth and as fifth element, as arcane substance and seed-bed, as nigredo, in Genesis and the body, and beside the other elements.

sections.title: Fourth or fifth
sections.line: Earth as the fifth element and as the fourth in the Axiom of Maria: CW14 ¶249 and ¶656.

quotes.quote: Earth occupies the central position as the fifth element, though it is not the quintessence and goal of the work but rather its basis, corresponding to terra as the arcane substance in Western alchemy.
The synthesis of the incorruptible One or quintessence follows the Axiom of Maria, the earth representing the “fourth.”
Fire comes at the beginning and is acted on by nothing, and earth at the end acts on nothing.
Between fire and earth there is no interaction; hence the four elements do not constitute a circle, i.e., a totality.

sections.title: Arcane substance and seed-bed
sections.line: Earth as arcane substance, prima materia and black earth: CW14 ¶632; CW12 ¶444 and ¶433.

quotes.quote: The alchemical earth, as we saw, is the arcane substance, here equated with the body of Christ and with adamah, the red earth of paradise.
According to Basilius Valentinus, the earth (as prima materia) is not a dead body, but is inhabited by a spirit that is its life and soul.
It is then the black earth in which the gold or the lapis is sown like the grain of wheat

sections.title: Nigredo as terra nigra
sections.line: The nigredo as terra nigra: CW14 ¶264, ¶729 and ¶244.

quotes.quote: The opus is far from having come to an end at this point, for the nigredo (terra nigra) still prevails and the substance of the stone is still black.
In our context the interpretation of the nigredo as terra (earth)
What remains below in the retort is our salt, that is, our earth, and it is of a black colour, a dragon that eats his own tail.

sections.title: Genesis, Adam and the body
sections.line: Earth in Genesis, in Adam and in Barnaud's scheme: CW14 ¶729, ¶552 and ¶59.

quotes.quote: It is the earth which, in Genesis, appeared out of the waters
Dryness came to him from the earth, moisture from the water, heat from the spirit, and cold from the soul.
Here Barnaud is rather more subtle, for he equates heaven with the soul, earth with the body, and water with the spirit,139 and thus arrives at the idea of the wholeness of a living organism.

sections.title: Beside the other elements; the Chinese fifth
sections.line: Earth beside the other elements, and the number five in China: CW13 pdf p249; CW14 ¶2; CW9ii ¶396; von Franz, Number and Time, pdf p135.

quotes.quote: Two of his elements are passive, earth and water, and two active, air
The toad “is the opposite of air, it is a contrary element, namely earth, whereon alone it moves by slow steps, and does not trust itself to another element.
Fire as spiritual, the other elements material; earth unmoving, the others moving.
In China the number five stands for the element of the earth carrying and centering all things at the center of the foundations of existence.
